scope: Bounded review of the 11 supplied primary papers; 15 supplied record IDs and six slice IDs retained.

primarySources.note: The deterministic theorem includes degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring through CLP shattering; preserve that stated contract.
Theorem 1 colors a high-degree subset with local failure Δ^{-c}; setting the degree upper bound to n yields simultaneous high-degree coverage. Theorem 2 completes all vertices.
Randomized Δ+1-list coloring; retains the exact degree-dependent historical formula.
Randomized Δ+1-list coloring reduces to deterministic degree+1-list coloring on polylogarithmic-size graphs. Keep Det_d symbolic rather than assigning an invented exponent.
The LOCAL deterministic bound applies to degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring with global high probability.

Full Δ+1-list coloring requires maximum degree at least log^{2+δ}n for fixed δ>0. Theorem is stronger CONGEST. HKNT22 incorporates this report's LOCAL work; do not count it as an independent frontier.
Sufficiently large Δ; q≥Δ−k_Δ+1. Output is a valid q-coloring or a local non-colorability certificate. The exceptional Δ≥log^{50}n regime is faster. No imported boundary hardness.
Three-coloring an n-cycle takes at least (log* n−3)/2 rounds. Use only the deterministic case here, even with a consistent orientation. No all-degree/palette lower projection.

Strict sampled-edge upper: Δ≥C log⁴n, O(log²Δ) rounds. The all-degree O(log²Δ+log³log n) implementation may retain original edges in its low-degree branch. The lower remains for sampled cliques with Bernoulli palette sampling and success 2/3, not ordinary LOCAL.
Full journal theorem confirms O(Δ)+(1/2)log* n rounds for ordinary Δ+1 coloring. Specializing Δ=2 supplies the cycle upper in the reference inset.
Set conflict degree d=1 in Theorem 4.1: lists of size degree(v)+1 suffice; exact bound is O(√Δ log^{5/2}Δ)+log* n.

corrections: Removed every original numerical palette-ratio/ordinal-degree-exponent projection; formulas depend jointly on n and Δ and are not universally ranked.
GG24 deterministic theorem, GK21 deterministic theorem, and FHK16 general theorem support degree+1 lists; records now show their strongest verified contract.
FHK16 uses exact O(√Δ log^{5/2}Δ)+log* n; CLP20 retains Det_d rather than an invented polynomial.
HKNT22 high-degree theorem is a partial-output statement unless every vertex meets the threshold. HNT21 instead colors the full graph with Δ+1 lists under a maximum-degree threshold.
FHJM26 requires sufficiently large Δ and gives coloring or a non-colorability certificate, with a separate Δ≥log^{50}n specialization.
Linial92 is shown only for deterministic three-coloring cycles; the upper reuses BEK14 at Δ=2. No all-degree or arbitrary-palette lower projection.
FGHKN24 lower applies to sampled-color communication, with precise Bernoulli sampling and success 2/3 on cliques; it is not an unrestricted LOCAL bound.
HNT21 remains identified as its original preprint, noting that HKNT22 incorporates its LOCAL work; published-only hides the original preprint marker.
The sparse-network upper's §4.2 alternate implementation uses palette-sampled edges; §5 retains original edges in the already-polylog-degree case.

The plotted sampled-network upper is restricted to the large-degree strict sampled-edge branch. Preserve the all-degree mixed-network implementation under the same original result ID as an inspectable variant.

boundedDerivations.claim: At Δ=2 the same algorithm computes a three-coloring in O(log* n). Combining with Linial92 Theorem 2.1 gives the cycle reference Θ(log* n).
Conflict degree d=1 gives degree(v)+1 lists and O(√Δ log^{5/2}Δ)+log* n.
Set the maximum-degree upper bound to n and union-bound per-vertex n^{-c} failure; target degree(v)≥log⁷n is simultaneously colored.
